newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end weak on Deng concerns but off lows.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end weak on Deng concerns but off lows.

text.p: Concerns about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping sent Hong Kong stocks tumbling on Tuesday, but the blue-chip Hang Seng Index managed to crawl back from its lows to finish only modestly weaker.
The index closed at 13,102.94, off 41.68 points or 0.32 percent. It hit a morning low of 12,933.98 points.
Turnover was HK$7.55 billion compared with HK$7.42 billion on Monday.
"There is some confusion over what his state of health is," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"Things look a little rough through this week."
Chinese sources said on Monday that Deng's deteriorating health had forced Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders to cut short provincial trips to return to Beijing.
Concerns about Deng's condition contributed to a 547-point slide in the Hang Seng Index last week. Rumours about the state of his health resurface from time to time.
"What is alarming is the extent to which it has lingered over the past trading sessions," said Fernow. "People are more nervous than they have been in the past."
China's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday there had been no major change in the health of 92-year-old Deng.
"That helped sentiment," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. But he said plummeting share prices in Shenzhen and Shanghai "cast a shadow over the market".
The Shenzhen B-share index tumbled 14.59 points, or 9.58 percent, to close at 137.72. In Shanghai, the B-share index dropped 4.754 points, or 6.97 percent, to 63.455.
Some brokers said an absence of interest in the Hong Kong market, even at lower levels, was worrying.
"The market needs to come back to get a lot of people buying it," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
But analysts said they had been encouraged by the Hang Seng's ability to close above 13,000 points.
"We were hoping that the support level would stay at 13,000 and I think it has. That has been a pretty firm level," said Fernow.
February Hang Seng Index futures fell 85 points to 13,120.
Among the major blue chips, HSBC Holdings fell HK$1.00 to HK$183.50, Henderson Land dropped HK$0.50 to HK$69.00 and Swire Pacific ended off HK$0.50 at HK$64.00.
